terms.gloss: first, firstly, in the first place
terms.grammar: adverb; followed by deinde, tum, postrēmō
evidence: Caes. B.G. 1.25: Caesar prīmum suō, deinde omnium ē cōnspectū remōtīs equīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The first of a series of points or acts: prīmum … deinde … tum … postrēmō (see secondly). prīmum omnium is “first of all”. prīmō is “at first”, as against later (prīmō … deinde), and stands for prīmum in lists mostly after Augustus (Lewis & Short).
What comes before everything else in importance: “above all”.

phrases.latin: prīmum est dēvium, deinde ab Autrōniō et cēterīs quadriduī, deinde sine tē.
phrases.english: Firstly, it’s off the road; secondly, it’s four days from Autronius and the rest; and thirdly, it’s without you.
first of all, I am awake myself

phrases.latin: ante omnia nē sit vitiōsus sermō nūtrīcibus
phrases.english: above all, the nurses’ speech must be free of faults

phrases.latin: hoc ante omnia fac, mī Lūcīlī: disce gaudēre
phrases.english: do this before all else, my Lucilius: learn to be glad

sources: Lewis & Short: primus · Lewis & Short: primum · Lewis & Short: primo
Quintilian and Seneca from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-quintilianus, loci-seneca-epistulae); Cicero (Att. 3.7.1) as in the record secondly; the other passages as Lewis & Short quotes them.
